confidence_notes: I based beer and cappuccino on aggregated cost-of-living sources (mylifeelsewhere, whereandwhen, freenance). They put a cappuccino at about 15–20 RON (~USD 3.4–4.0) and a domestic draft beer at about 15 RON (~USD 3.3–3.5). The restaurant meal figures are less certain. The sources disagree a lot: one says USD 4 for an inexpensive meal and USD 10 for a mid-range meal for two, which looks implausibly low, while CityCost gives a mid-range dinner for two at USD 32–74. I used model judgement within that range. I did not search cocktail and wine prices directly. I estimated them from how they usually compare with local beer prices in Romanian city-centre bars, so they are less certain. The accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July (peak summer and festival season, such as Untold in early August). I did not check booking pages for them. The FX figure is the RBA 4pm reference rate for 18 November 2026, as reported in search results that cite the RBA.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Cluj-Napoca with Romania's second-tier university and IT cities and with central-eastern European cities such as Brașov, Timișoara and Debrecen. Cluj is one of Romania's most expensive cities after Bucharest, and its restaurant prices are roughly 20–25% above the national average.
